capital_and_geographical_region: Dispur; North-Eastern Region (Brahmaputra and Barak river valleys)
international_borders: Bhutan to the north; Bangladesh to the west and south (along with the strategic Siliguri Corridor gateway)
historical_and_cultural_heritage: Ahom Dynasty (who repelled the Mughal Empire at the Battle of Saraighat in 1671 led by Lachit Borphukan), Bihu dance, Kamakhya Temple, Assamese Classical Language
major_geographical_features: Brahmaputra River, Majuli River Island, Karbi Anglong and Cachar Hills, Mikir Hills
economic_and_resource_significance: Assam Tea (GI tag, contributes over 50% of India's tea), oldest operational oil refinery in Asia at Digboi, Muga golden silk
special_constitutional_provisions: Sixth Schedule of the Constitution (Bodoland, Karbi Anglong, and Dima Hasao Autonomous District Councils); Article 371B
strategic_and_geopolitical_importance: Anchor state for India's 'Act East Policy', vital transit hub connecting the seven northeastern sister states to the mainland via the Chicken's Neck

capital_and_geographical_region: Thiruvananthapuram; Coastal Plains & Southern Western Ghats (Malabar and Coromandel fringe)
international_borders: Coastline along the Arabian Sea (no international land boundaries)
historical_and_cultural_heritage: Chera Dynasty, Kingdom of Travancore (Marthanda Varma defeated the Dutch East India Company at the Battle of Colachel in 1741), Kathakali, Kalaripayattu, Malayalam Classical Language
major_geographical_features: Anamudi Peak (highest peak in South India at 2,695 m), Palghat Gap, Vembanad Lake (longest lake in India / Ramsar site), Ashtamudi Lake
economic_and_resource_significance: 'Spice Coast of India' (Cardamom, Black Pepper), Natural Rubber (leads national production >70%), Coconut, coir manufacturing, monazite mineral beach sands
special_constitutional_provisions: Decentralized Panchayati Raj planning under the People's Plan Campaign, high Human Development Index (HDI)
strategic_and_geopolitical_importance: Dominates busy international Indian Ocean trade lanes, home to the Southern Naval Command (Kochi) and Vizhinjam International Transshipment Deepwater Seaport

capital_and_geographical_region: Leh and Kargil; Trans-Himalayas (Cold High-Altitude Desert Plateau)
international_borders: Pakistan-administered Kashmir to the west/northwest (Line of Control); China (Tibet / Xinjiang) along the Line of Actual Control (LAC)
historical_and_cultural_heritage: Namgyal Dynasty of Ladakh, Tibetan Buddhist monastic architecture (Hemis, Thiksey Gompas), Losar festival, historical Silk Route trade crossroads
major_geographical_features: Karakoram Range, Siachen Glacier, Zanskar Range, Pangong Tso Lake, Tso Moriri Lake, Indus River, Khardung La Pass
economic_and_resource_significance: Pashmina wool extraction (Changthangi goats), solar and geothermal power potential (Puga valley), apricot horticulture (Raktsey Karpo GI)
special_constitutional_provisions: Union Territory without legislature (governed directly under the J&K Reorganisation Act 2019); Ladakh Autonomous Hill Development Councils (LAHDC Leh & Kargil)
strategic_and_geopolitical_importance: Most sensitive northern military sector containing Daulat Beg Oldi (DBO airstrip), Galwan Valley, Depsang Plains, and the Siachen Glacier tri-junction

capital_and_geographical_region: Gandhinagar; Western India (Kathiawar Peninsula, Kutch, and alluvial mainland plains)
international_borders: Land and maritime border with Pakistan (Sindh province / Sir Creek tidal estuary)
historical_and_cultural_heritage: Indus Valley Civilization ports (Lothal, Dholavira UNESCO Site), Solanki Dynasty, Modhera Sun Temple, Garba dance, birthplace of Mahatma Gandhi and Sardar Patel
major_geographical_features: Longest coastline among Indian states (approx 1,600 km), Great Rann of Kutch (seasonal salt marsh), Girnar Hill, Gulf of Khambhat, Narmada and Tapi deltas
economic_and_resource_significance: Industrial power: Petroleum refining (Jamnagar), diamond cutting (Surat), chemical manufacturing, cotton production, groundnut crops, Mundra and Deendayal (Kandla) ports
special_constitutional_provisions: Article 371(2) providing for special developmental boards for Saurashtra, Kutch, and the rest of Gujarat
strategic_and_geopolitical_importance: Hosts India's largest private and public container ports; key energy infrastructure gateway handling crude imports; maritime security monitoring at Sir Creek

capital_and_geographical_region: Itanagar; Eastern Himalayan Mountain System (North-East Border)
international_borders: Tibet (China) along the McMahon Line to the north; Bhutan to the west; Myanmar to the east
historical_and_cultural_heritage: Tawang Monastery (second largest Tibetan Buddhist monastery in the world), indigenous tribal councils (Kebang of the Adis), Losar, Torgya festivals
major_geographical_features: Kangto peak, Namcha Barwa tri-junction, Sela Pass, Bum La Pass, Dihang/Brahmaputra gorge, Subansiri, Lohit, and Dibang river valleys
economic_and_resource_significance: Highest hydroelectric power potential in India, dense tropical and sub-alpine forest timber, kiwi fruit horticulture, diverse medicinal biodiversity
special_constitutional_provisions: Article 371H (special discretionary powers for the Governor on law and order); Bengal Eastern Frontier Regulation 1873 (Inner Line Permit / ILP)
strategic_and_geopolitical_importance: Frontline border defense buffer; historical site of the 1962 Sino-Indian War; safeguarded by key infrastructure projects like Sela Tunnel and the Trans-Arunachal Highway
